Read a myDAR walk

Source: R/mydar_read.R
read_mydar_walk.Rd

Reads the files a myDAR walk produces into plain data frames that the mydar_*_view() functions plot. read_mydar_walk() reads a whole output directory; the other functions read one file each.

Usage

read_mydar_walk(dir, max_points = 20000, max_cells = 40000, local = TRUE)

read_mydar_points(path, max_points = 20000)

read_mydar_terrain(path, max_cells = 40000)

read_mydar_orthophoto(path, max_pixels = 4e+06)

read_mydar_gpkg(path)

read_mydar_trajectory(path)

Arguments

dir

Path to a walk output directory.

max_points

Most points to keep from the cloud. Larger clouds are thinned by taking every k-th point in file order, which keeps the relative point density across the walk. Use Inf to keep every point.

max_cells

Most DEM cells to keep. A larger DEM is aggregated by the smallest whole factor that brings it under the limit (cell mean).

local

If TRUE (default), every spatial table is moved to walk-local coordinates by subtraction only: x and y become meters from a whole-meter origin at the south-west corner of the walk, and z becomes height above the lowest DEM (ground) cell, or above the lowest ground-class point when the walk has no DEM. The subtracted origin is kept in $origin (x, y, z); add it back to recover project coordinates. trajectory.csv is in its own local frame (meters east, north and up of the first GPS fix) and is left as written.

path

Path to one walk file.

max_pixels

Most orthophoto pixels to keep; a larger image is averaged down by the smallest whole factor that fits.

Value

read_mydar_walk() returns a mydar_walk list with

points

One row per kept point: point_id (row in the file), x, y, z, class (LAS code), class_name, sigma_m (the file's per-point 1-sigma, per axis, in meters), source ("LiDAR" or "camera") and, when the cloud is colored, r, g, b (0-255).

terrain

One row per DEM cell with a height: x, y (cell center) and z. Attribute cell_size holds the cell width and height.

track

Track vertices in walk order: vertex, x, y, z.

track_points

Once-a-second track samples with t_s and map_95_m, the 95% map-position radius at that time.

gps_fixes

GPS fixes with t_s, h_acc_m, used, residual_m, residual_95_m and map_95_m.

pins

Control pins placed on the walk.

features

Named list, one data frame per feature layer, one row per vertex (fid, vertex, x, y, z and the layer's attributes).

accuracy

The one-row accuracy table.

orthophoto

From orthophoto.tif: png, the image as PNG bytes with no georeference or metadata, and extent, c(xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) in the walk's coordinates.

trajectory

Poses from trajectory.csv with t_s (seconds from the first pose).

crs

The project CRS, e.g. "EPSG:32612".

origin

The x/y/z origin subtracted when local = TRUE, else c(x = 0, y = 0, z = 0).

The single-file readers return the matching element.

Details

A walk directory holds walk.copc.laz (the point cloud), terrain.tif (the DEM), orthophoto.tif, walk.gpkg (track, GPS fixes, pins, features and the accuracy table) and trajectory.csv (the device poses). Walks recorded without LiDAR have no point cloud or DEM; those parts of the result are NULL.

The readers need packages that myIO does not install: rlas for the point cloud, terra for the DEM and orthophoto and sf for the GeoPackage.

See also

mydar_dashboard and the other mydar_*_view() functions; mydar_iphone_walk for a walk that needs none of the optional packages.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
walk <- read_mydar_walk("path/to/walk", max_points = 20000)
walk
mydar_dashboard(walk)
} # }
